learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and key terms of automated docker builds.

content.intro: This lesson covers Automated Docker Builds. You will connect the named subtopics from the supplied Docker curriculum to a small, observable example. Work through the visual first, then use the example to form a prediction and check it against the actual behavior.
content.why_it_matters: An image-delivery pipeline should use repeatable inputs, build once per release candidate where appropriate, test image behavior, scan according to policy, publish explicit tags, retain provenance, and verify the exact artifact before deployment. A green build is not a substitute for deployment and rollback checks. Learning automated docker builds helps you make deployment behavior explicit and repeatable instead of relying on a command that happened to work on one machine.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: Start with the supplied example for automated docker builds. Before running it, state what you expect to happen. Compare the real output with that prediction, then change one variable or setting in a disposable lab to test the boundary of the idea. If a command is not supported on your operating system or installed Docker version, consult the linked official reference and record the actual version rather than guessing.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Automated Docker Builds
content_blocks.code:
docker build --progress=plain -t codeleaf-demo:local .
docker image inspect codeleaf-demo:local
content_blocks.expected_output: The build output shows steps and cache decisions; inspection confirms the resulting local image metadata.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run from a folder with a valid Dockerfile and application files. Change the tag when it would collide with an existing lab image.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Remove `codeleaf-demo:local` only if you created it for this exercise and no longer need it.
content_blocks.safety_note: Run only against a local test Docker environment. Docker commands are not executed by the CodeLeaf lesson page.
content_blocks.limitations: CodeLeaf currently does not execute Docker Engine, Docker Compose, build, networking, or host-administration commands from lesson pages. Use the example as inspectable material and run only in an approved local lab. Production services and arbitrary learner commands must never run inside the FastAPI web process.
content_blocks.schema_assumptions: Confirm the installed Docker Engine, CLI, Compose, and Buildx versions and the target OS before using version- or platform-sensitive options.

content_blocks.title: Practical checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Keep this lesson in draft while reviewing: Automated Docker Builds. Capture the command/configuration, expected and actual result, one failure or edge case, and cleanup performed. This course does not award XP from content files; CodeLeaf backend rules remain authoritative.

task: Apply automated docker builds to a small local case. Record the configuration or command, expected result, observed result, one limitation/edge case, and how you verified the result.
hints: Begin with read-only inspection commands and identify the active Docker context before any mutating action.
Use a disposable name, local test image, and synthetic data; change one thing at a time.
If the outcome differs, preserve the exact error and logs, check the official reference for your installed version, and document the verified fix.
expected_output: The build output shows steps and cache decisions; inspection confirms the resulting local image metadata.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming that a successful start means the application is ready.
common_mistakes.why: A container can start while its dependent service is unavailable or the application is failing after startup.
common_mistakes.fix: Inspect health/status and logs; add a meaningful health check or retry strategy where appropriate.

common_mistakes.problem: Keeping required data only in the container writable layer.
common_mistakes.why: Replacing the container can discard that layer and its application state.
common_mistakes.fix: Select a named volume or an external storage system, then rehearse a restore.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a command without checking context, target, or permissions.
common_mistakes.why: Docker commands affect the active endpoint and can change host resources or publish services.
common_mistakes.fix: Check `docker context show`, use an isolated lab, make the smallest change, and verify the resulting state.
